findings.title: Metric accounting for cleared/dropped connections verified correct (no double-decrement)
findings.claim: Each cleared or dropped connection is decremented once; connections dropped from excess_connections or the old conns don't get decremented a second time when their error futures fire.

findings.title: many_connections test fails with ConnectTimeout opening 400 connections
findings.claim: The many_connections test fails with ConnectTimeout; the PR doesn't touch this code path, so the reviewer believes it's likely an environment problem, but did not confirm this by running the test on main.

findings.title: Keyspace (USE) failure logging demoted from warn! to debug!
findings.claim: The old code warned when USE failed; now a repeated failure is only visible at debug level, which is worse when the pool is non-empty because nothing is published to shared_conns, making the failure invisible while the pool keeps opening connections and failing USE with backoff.

findings.title: ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace ignores evt.requested_shard, growing backoff without…
findings.claim: Unlike the old Connection error arm which retried a failed shard-aware attempt once on the regular port without setting had_error_since_last_refill, the new arm always sets had_error_since_last_refill (growing backoff) and never falls back to a non-shard-aware attempt, delaying refills more than a shard-aware connect failure does.

findings.title: Moving keyspace check ahead of shard-info handling delays learning the sharder
findings.claim: block_advanced_shard_awareness, maybe_reshard, and the shard-aware-port update now wait until USE completes; if USE keeps failing on a node (e.g., missing keyspace there), the pool never learns the node's sharding or shard-aware port and stays on the old topology, going through the non-shard-aware path on every refill. This looks intentional given a test name but is not mentioned in the PR description.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for shard-aware retry behavior and non-empty-pool USE failure
findings.claim: No test checks the shard-aware retry behaviour described in the requested_shard finding, and none checks that a failed USE on a non-empty pool doesn't overwrite shared_conns with Broken; the only failure-path test with an empty pool runs the handler directly, not through run().
